Clay wants you to get about the same results whether you use its own agent or point Claude Code at Clay. Usage is already split close to 50/50 between Clay’s agent and outside harnesses. In this episode, we chat with Jeff Barg, Head of AI at Clay, about what it takes to build go-to-market infrastructure that any agent can use. Jeff joined Clay when it acquired Avenue , the ops alerting startup he cofounded. At the time, Clay had about 50 people, and Avenue had five. AI was already a big part of how Clay thought about its product, but nobody there worked on AI. Since then, the business has grown roughly 10x, and the team is up to around 600 people. In September, Clay raised $115 million at a $7.1 billion valuation . By Jeff’s napkin math, it would cost about $1,500 to check all 40 million companies in Clay’s database against your ideal customer profile with a classifier like TypeSafe’s Jev. Models have been acing Clay’s lead-qualification evals for about a year now. Jeff sees more value in using frontier models for orchestration and deep research. We also talk about why customers hate picking a model, how Clay plans to pick one for them, and why the team still runs its agents on a system it built with BullMQ, without Temporal or LangGraph. Jeff tells us what happened when OpenAI called off Clay’s ChatGPT apps launch with two days to go. We get into why customers hated Workflows at first, how agents came to build most workflows, and when post-training pays off. rss.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
rss.summary: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025 . It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics. Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO . In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk you are plain out of luck. sqlite3_rsync can copy a snapshot of your database over an SSH connection to another machine, without first needing to create a full local copy! It's also good for synchronizing an existing copy of a database without re-transmitting the entire thing over the network. It works in a similar way to regular rsync: The core idea behind the protocol is that the replica sends cryptographic hashes for pages or groups of pages over to the origin side. The origin sends back page content that differs, or requests finer-grain hashes if a multi-page hash does not match. If the origin and replica start out being vastly different, the total network bandwidth can exceed the size of the entire database, due to the overhead of exchanging hashes, but the excess bandwidth is not great - a few percent at most. Update : Hah! Turns out I wrote about this application of sqlite_rsync back in October 2024 when the tool was first released. Tags: backups , sqlite

rss.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
rss.summary: My comment on The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features — Hacker News. I had a NYT photographer take my picture at my home earlier this year (for a story about Moltbook, oddly enough). At one point I asked if they could fix things up if I had a stain on my shirt and they said absolutely not - they present photographs as they were taken, with cropping and balancing applied but no edits beyond that. He did spend a bunch of time trying to find the best possible natural lighting for the shots he wanted. The photo at the top of https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/02/technology/moltbook-ai-so... is my laptop, taken in my garden, after hunting around for the best spot that didn't have too much glare on the screen. You can see how dirty my screen is, too! Photography for a newspaper is photo journalism, and they take it seriously. (Thankfully I did not have a visible stain on my shirt.) github.name: dagu
github.description: Self-hostable workflow orchestrator for teams whose main work isn't orchestration. Declarative YAML over your scripts, SSH commands, containers, etc; keep workflows separate from business logic. One binary, no database, runs on limited H/W resources. Alternative to Airflow / Cron / Job Scheduler.
github.text_excerpt:
Docs · CLI · API · Examples · Live demo (username/password: demouser) · Discord

Dagu

Dagu is a local-first workflow engine for operations and internal automation. It is open source and self-hostable: a single binary with a built-in Web UI, no external database or message broker, running on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Define [DAGs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed_acyclic_graph) in a declarative YAML format. It natively supports shell commands, Docker containers, Kubernetes Jobs, remote commands via SSH, and more through Dagu Actions. Dagu turns existing scripts and runbooks into production workflows with scheduling, retries, human tasks, and run history. It runs where your data and credentials live: on-prem, air-gapped, edge, or cloud, and scales from a single node to a fleet of workers. **Highlights:** - Single binary installation. - Self-contained: no external DBMS or message broker required. - Runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows. - Declarative YAML format for defining DAGs. - Run existing shell commands, Docker containers, Kubernetes Jobs, and remote commands over SSH without modifications. - Compose reusable Sub-DAGs and run work in parallel with concurrency controls. - Schedule workflows with cron syntax, timezones, overlap policies, and catch-up windows. - Keep logs, run history, retries, notifications, and webhook triggers in one place. - Built-in MCP server for inspecting workflows and runs, maintaining Wiki pages, applying changes, and controlling runs. - Optional monitoring in Dagu Console: every server's runs and trends in one place, and an email when a workflow fails or a server stops reporting. Opt-in, outbound HTTPS only, metadata only. ## Quick Look For a quick look at how workflows are defined, see the examples.

github.text_excerpt:
# m365-copilot-proxy Use Microsoft 365 Copilot as an LLM backend for OpenAI-compatible coding agents like [pi](https://pi.dev/) and [OpenClaw](https://docs.openclaw.ai/). Wraps M365 Copilot's WebSocket/SignalR API in an OpenAI-compatible interface with tool calling support. > **Want the gory protocol details?** See [docs/m365-copilot-api.md](docs/m365-copilot-api.md) — a full write-up of M365 Copilot's undocumented WebSocket API: auth, SignalR frames, tones/models, throttling, the "Disengaged" filter, and the Copilot Studio agent trick that makes tool calling work. ## How it works M365 Copilot uses a SignalR WebSocket protocol, not the OpenAI API. This project translates between the two: 1. **Standalone proxy** — HTTP server with `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/models` endpoints. Works with any OpenAI-compatible client (pi, OpenClaw, etc.). 2. **OpenClaw plugin** — Config generator + setup CLI for OpenClaw's provider system. ### Tool calling M365 Copilot doesn't support OpenAI-style `tool_calls` natively. Instead, tools are emulated via a **Markdown-fence format** (the JSON `{"tool":...}` format was removed — it scored 0/5 on real agentic tasks; see [hypotheses §9](docs/hypotheses.md)): - Tool definitions are injected into the prompt as fenced templates inside a `<tools>` block - The model emits a fenced tool call — a code block whose info-string is the tool name (scalar args as `key: value` header lines, one free-form body arg as the fence body, `old`/`new` edits as aider-style `SEARCH/REPLACE` diffs) - The proxy/handler parses that and converts it to OpenAI `tool_calls` format - **Shell-routing (the key lever):** M365's chat-tuned model won't "act as an agent" on demand but *will* reflexively write a ```` ```bash ```` block. When the toolset includes a shell tool (`bash`/`shell`/`run`/`run_command`/… — any name), the proxy injects "do the whole step by writing one ```` ```bash ```` block" framing and routes that block to the shell tool. This exploits the one agentic behavior Microsoft's system prompt permits, and is what turns 0/5 into real multi-turn loops (verified 9-tool-call bug fix). - **Reliability comes from the Copilot Studio agent (below) + the fenced/shell framing** — without the agent, M365 ignores tool instructions and answers in prose ### Agent mode On first use, the system creates a **Copilot Studio agent** with tool-calling instructions bake

Foundry

Instantaneous CUDA graph restoration via execution context materialization.

Foundry is a system that persists CUDA graph states through *template-based context materialization*. It materializes both the structure and execution context of captured CUDA graphs, making graph restoration kernel-agnostic and eliminating the need for hand-crafted patching rules. By intercepting CUDA driver calls, Foundry enforces a **deterministic memory layout** and automatically detects and serializes the **binaries of kernels** used in the CUDA graphs. With Foundry, LLM serving engines can directly reload CUDA states from disk and skip the warmup process to start in a few seconds. ## Foundry in Action Demonstration of serving `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8` with expert parallel size = 2.

Baseline vLLM (top) vs. vLLM + Foundry (bottom). Foundry reconstructs 256 graphs in 1 sec (plus ~2 sec sampler warmup + API server init), while original vLLM spends around 30 sec to warmup and capture graphs.

| 🛡️ 官方接口，不碰风控 | 🎚️ 逐条权限，不整群一刀切 | 🧠 三层记忆，跨重启不丢 | 🔌 四步一键接入 | | ------------------------------ | ------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------- | | 走 QQ 开放平台 + 外接协议直连，不 hook 客户端 | 每句先判身份再收工具，认不出一律最低档 | 事实 / 日记 / 知识图谱，凌晨自动巩固 | 首次启动向导 + 一键直连自动生成密钥和端口 | ![dsh-roost 概览页](docs/images/overview.png) > **侧栏「概览」页**：最上面是接入进度与一键启动，接着是六格状态（托管会话 / 今日 Token / 排队并发 / 缓存命中 / 最近一轮 / 工具挂载）、近 7 天用量、8 周活跃度、Token 构成与耗时拆分、会话卡片与筛选，最后是快捷、端口与最近动态。所有用量只统计 dsh-roost 自己创建的会话。换图要求见 [docs/images/README.md](docs/images/README.md)。 --- ## 它做什么 给每个 QQ 会话建一个长期存在的 DSH 会话——一个群、一个私聊各对应一个，断线重连、重启之后映射还在。之后的每一轮： 1. **认人**：判断这句话是谁说的，按档位收好这一轮能用的工具 2. **交给 DSH**：把消息送进对应会话，等 AI 说完；工具、记忆、上下文压缩、人格都由 DSH 提供 3. **送回去**：通过框架外接协议回话，分几段说、配图、发语音、要不要收尾，都由模型自己调工具决定 能力从哪来，一眼看清： | 你要的能力 | 由谁提供 | | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | 收发 QQ 消息、语音 ASR、引用 / 合并转发、切段、防吵（冷却 / 配额 / 认领） | [Roost](https://github.com/roost-qq/qq-bot-roost) 框架的外接协议 `roost-host/1` | | 会话、工具（文件 / 命令）、三层记忆、上下文压缩、人格 | DSH | | 会话映射、逐条权限、侧栏面板、一键接入、主动搭话与排期 | **dsh-roost** | **为什么值得接**：让 QQ 消息直接进 DSH 会话之后，AI 不只能聊天，还能用 DSH 的工具（文件、命令）、三层记忆、上下文压缩——这是这一层接入存在的全部理由。

![Varro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/koltyakov/varro/main/assets/banner.jpg) # Varro: OpenCode Workbench [![Visual Studio Marketplace](https://badgen.net/vs-marketplace/v/koltyakov.varro?color=0078d4)](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=koltyakov.varro) [![Open VSX Version](https://badgen.net/open-vsx/version/koltyakov/varro?color=a66f00&label=Open%20VSX)](https://open-vsx.org/extension/koltyakov/varro) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2ea44f.svg)](https://github.com/koltyakov/varro/blob/main/LICENSE) Varro runs [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) inside VS Code. It adds project-aware chat, parallel sessions, plan and change review, model and permission controls, commit-message generation, and usage reports. **Supports OpenCode v2 and v1.** Varro automatically detects the connected API and uses the same workbench for either version. OpenCode v2 is recommended for new installations. OpenCode remains responsible for agents, providers, models, commands, skills, MCP servers, and their configuration. Varro reads that configuration and provides a VS Code interface for it. ![The Varro OpenCode workbench in VS Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/koltyakov/varro/main/assets/demo.png) ## Quick start 1. [Install Varro](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=koltyakov.varro). 2. Install [OpenCode v2](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/). On macOS, Linux, or WSL, run `npm install -g @opencode/cli`. On native Windows, download the standalone CLI. 3. Connect a provider with `opencode auth login` or `/connect` in Varro. 4. Open a folder, select `Varro` in the Secondary Side Bar, and start a session. You can also run `Varro: Focus Chat` from the Command Palette. Varro handles the server connection. Install OpenCode where Varro runs: the Windows CLI for native Windows, or inside WSL for a WSL window. Add it to `PATH` or set `varro.server.command` to its executable path. Already using v1? Keep it, or see [choosing and updating OpenCode](https://github.com/koltyakov/varro/blob/main/docs/usage.md#choose-and-update-opencode) to switch versions. After switching, let active work finish and run `Varro: Restart Server`. Check the status bar for the connected version; see [recovery steps](https://github.com/koltyakov/varro/blob/main/docs/usage.md#if-restart-does-not-switch-to-v2) if it still shows v1.
